text: Relatively untrained individuals can benefit from a substantial energy surplus (~2,000 kcal/ day); in this population, body mass gains are predominantly achieved by increasing fat-free mass at the expense of body fat, at least over the short term. In well-trained subjects, evidence suggests that a positive energy balance of 500 to 1,000 kcal/day is preferable for increasing fatfree mass (42). It has been suggested that even smaller surpluses (200 to 300 kcal/day) may be more appropriate for well-trained individuals who want to minimize body fat deposition (42).
